COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS 
06.09.2023 WPPIL No. 136 of 2023 
Hon’ble Vipin Sanghi, C.J.
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Navnish Negi, learned counsel for 
the petitioner. 
2. The Uttarakhand State Legal Services 
Authority has preferred the present writ 
petition, in public interest, highlighting the 
serious situation existing in relation to the 
Raaji tribes residing in the State of 
Uttarakhand. 
3. The District Legal Services Authority has 
conducted a survey of the said tribes by 
visiting the several villages occupied by 
them, and compiled the data which has been 
placed on record. 
4. The said data shows that the population 
of the Raaji tribes has sharply declined over 
the years. The factors relevant to determine
their development indicate that the State has 
not taken enough steps to provide even basic 
facilities in the villages where the said tribe
resides. The distribution of the population in 
the villages occupied by the Raaji tribes show that there are hardly any survivors beyond 
the age of 55 years. The life expectancy 
amongst the members of the said tribe is, 
therefore, very low. 
5. Mr. Negi points out that even Primary 
Health Centers are situated at distances of 
about 25 Kms. from the villages where the 
said tribes reside, and there are hardly any 
educational facilities available to them. 
6. Mr. Negi has also drawn attention of the 
Court to the Scheduled Tribes and Other 
Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of 
Forest Rights) Act, 2006 and, in particular, to 
Section 3(2) thereof to submit that there can 
be no excuse for the State Government not 
to take developmental activities for setting
up dispensaries, hospitals, schools etc. in the 
villages occupied by the Raaji tribe. 
7. Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, learned Standing
Counsel for the Union of India, accepts notice 
on behalf of respondent No. 1. 
8. Ms. Puja Banga, learned Brief Holder for 
the State, accepts notice on behalf of 
respondent Nos. 2 to 7. 
9. We direct the respondent No. 1, as well 
as respondent Nos. 2 and 3 to urgently look  into the situation aforesaid, and to take 
remedial steps without waiting for any 
further orders. 
10. The respondents should file their 
affidavits disclosing the steps that they have 
taken, and they propose to take, with 
timeline to remedy the situation aforesaid. 
11. List the matter on 06.11.2023. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) (Vipin Sanghi, C.J.)
 06.09.2023 06.09.2023

19.02.2024 WPPIL No. 136 of 2023
Hon’ble Ritu Bahri, C.J.
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Navnish Negi, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. V.K. Kapruwan, learned Standing Counsel for 
the Union of India/ respondent no. 1. 
3. Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Chief Standing Counsel 
assisted by Mr. Gajendra Tripathi, learned Standing 
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/ respondent nos. 
2, 3, 5, 6 & 7. 
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties. 
5. Mr. Geeta Ram Nautiyal, Incharge Director, 
Social Welfare Department, Uttarakhand and Mr. 
Sanjay Tolia, Director, Tribal Welfare Department, 
Uttarakhand are present in Court today. On a specific 
query from the Court, they have informed the Court 
that plots have been allotted to 83 Tribals for 
constructing 134 houses, and budget under the 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojna had already been 
sanctioned in the year 2021-22. A specific query has 
been put to the respondents, as to whether electricity
and water connection have been given in the area, 
where plots have been allotted. 
6. At this stage, counsel appearing for the 
Uttarakhand State Legal Services Authority submits 
that they will also, through their paralegals, conduct a 
survey, and inform this Court that apart from 83  Tribals, how many other Tribals are still landless.
7. Counsel for the respondents, representing State 
seeks time to file affidavit. Respondents will file a 
better affidavit giving details, whether benefit of social 
welfare schemes is being extended to these Tribals. 
Especially with regard to mid-day meals, an order has 
been given to the respondents, whereby in the entire 
State of Haryana, one bottle milk is being given since 
COVID-19 to all children as mid-day meal. In the 
affidavit, the respondents will also give details of other 
mid-day meals. The affidavit shall be filed within two 
weeks. 
8. List on 06.03.2024.
9. Copy of this order be given to the counsel for the 
State. 
10. Personal presence of Director, Social Welfare 
Department and Director, Tribal Welfare Department is 
exempted. 
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) (Ritu Bahri, C.J.)
